children: Most Gulf stock markets ended lower on Sunday as investors awaited indications on whether US President Donald Trump will order fresh attacks on Iran.

Blasts struck several sites across southern Iran on Saturday night, Qeshm Island among them, according to state broadcaster reports. The IRGC Navy then reported two burning tankers after mine strikes on a route it labelled as off-limits, though it is unclear whether the sea and land incidents are connected.
dropped 0.8%, weighed down by a 1.5% fall for Al Rajhi Bank
and a 1.3% decline for Saudi National Bank
, the country's biggest lender by assets.
The kingdom's Energy Ministry says debris from a foiled attack on Sunday hit an administrative office of Saudi Aramco in Riyadh, causing damage but no casualties.
Meanwhile, US Central Command says an American aircraft opened fire on and disabled a merchant ship that tried to defy the US blockade of Iran on Saturday.
Further west, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis says it downed two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh.
pared early losses to finish 0.5% down.
Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani told Al Jazeera on Saturday that Doha is still mediating between Washington and Tehran to keep the regional crisis from escalating.
Outside the Gulf, Egypt's blue-chip index
dropped 0.7%, dragged down by a 5.8% slide in Abu Qir Fertilizers
and a 5.9% retreat for Misr Fertilizers Production Co

Egypt has told its fertilizer makers that natural gas deliveries are being cut by another 33%, according to a company statement and industry officials on Sunday, as the government tries to reduce its reliance on costly liquefied natural gas imports.
Gas is both feedstock and fuel for Egypt's fertiliser producers.
